source: JZ Mock E · Paper 2 · Question 19 · Publisher worked answer
label: JZ Mock E · Paper 2 · Question 19
lead: Interpret Policy 1 as follows: even after learning the actual truth values of any four statements, at least two listed options must remain possible.
knowledgePattern: Apply an information policy to complete five-statement truth patterns
solution:
Use 1 for true and 0 for false, in the printed statement order. The options are A: 10101, B: 00101, C: 11101, D: 10001, E: 10111 and F: 10100.

Apply the stated clarification of Policy 1: even after learning the actual values of any four statements, at least two options remain possible. For a candidate actual pattern, choose which one position has not been checked. The only distinct pattern agreeing at the other four positions is obtained by changing that unchecked position. Thus every one-position change of the actual pattern must also be listed.

For A, changing positions 1, 2, 3, 4 or 5 gives B, C, D, E or F respectively. It therefore meets Policy 1. Each of B–F differs from A at one position. Changing any different position produces a pattern that differs from A at two positions, and none of those is listed. Each of B–F consequently fails the policy for some set of four checks.

Policy 1 also forces at least six options: the actual pattern and its five distinct one-position changes. The six printed options attain this bound, so Policy 2 is satisfied. A is the consistent actual pattern. Answer A.

hints.title: Represent an option by all five truth values
hints.body: Write each listed combination as a fixed-order row of five true/false entries.
hints.recap: Cover every relevant case and keep all conditions in the same case consistent.
hints.pitfall: Use the actual-response interpretation stated above the question.
hints.pause: For a chosen unchecked position, compare which rows agree in the other four positions.

recall.reminder: Cover every relevant case and keep all conditions in the same case consistent.

hints.title: Repeat the policy test at every possible unchecked position
hints.body: Test a proposed actual option after each possible choice of four checks. Ask whether a distinct listed option can still agree with everything learnt.
hints.recap: Consistency between several statements concerns one shared assignment, rather than different assignments chosen independently.
hints.pitfall: Possible ambiguity for one set of checked positions does not establish the policy for every set.
hints.pause: Determine which candidates satisfy all five tests, without selecting one from just a single test.

recall.reminder: Consistency between several statements concerns one shared assignment, rather than different assignments chosen independently.

hints.title: Justify the smallest possible list
hints.body: Count the distinct alternatives that the policy forces around any valid actual pattern, then compare this bound with the printed list.
hints.recap: To establish a least possible count, prove a lower bound and give an arrangement that attains it.
hints.pitfall: Alternatives required for different unchecked positions may need to be distinct; justify your count.
hints.pause: Verify both policies and identify the unique actual option.
